subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Simple Interest — Formula, Rate Finding and Multi-Step Problems (W12 B1)

questions.stem: Find the Simple Interest on Rs.1,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years.
questions.explanation: B is correct. SI = P×R×T/100 = 1000×5×2/100 = 10000/100 = Rs.100. Verify: 5% of 1000 = Rs.50 per year × 2 years = Rs.100 ✓. Trap: Rs.50 = interest for 1 year only; Rs.200 = interest for 4 years (confuses T=4 with T=2).

questions.stem: Find the Simple Interest on Rs.2,000 at 10% per annum for 3 years.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SI = P×R×T/100 = 2000×10×3/100 = 60000/100 = Rs.600. Verify: 10% of 2000 = Rs.200 per year × 3 years = Rs.600 ✓. Amount = P+SI = 2000+600 = Rs.2,600. Trap: Rs.400 = for 2 years; Rs.800 = for 4 years.

questions.stem: At what rate of interest will Rs.2,000 yield Rs.360 as Simple Interest in 3 years?
A sum of Rs.5,000 amounts to Rs.6,500 in 4 years at Simple Interest. Find the rate of interest per annum.
A sum of money doubles itself in 10 years at Simple Interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: C is correct. If sum doubles, Amount=2P, so SI=P. P = P×R×10/100 → R=100/10=10% per annum. Short rule: if sum doubles in T years at SI, R=100/T%. For T=10: R=100/10=10%. Verify: at 10% pa SI, P grows by 10%×P per year; in 10 years grows by 100% = doubles ✓. Trap: 5% → doubles in 20 years (not 10); 20% → doubles in 5 years.

questions.stem: Rs.4,000 is invested at 5% p.a. for 2 years and then at 7% p.a. for 3 more years. What is the total Simple Interest?
questions.explanation: C is correct. SI for first 2 years at 5%: 4000×5×2/100=400. SI for next 3 years at 7%: 4000×7×3/100=840. Total SI=400+840=Rs.1,240. Verify: 4000×0.05×2=400; 4000×0.07×3=840; 400+840=1240 ✓. Trap: Rs.1,200 = 4000×5×6/100=1200 (uses 5% throughout for all 5 years — ignores rate change).

questions.stem: Rs.10,000 is split equally and invested at 4% and 6% per annum for 2 years. What is the total Simple Interest earned?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Each half = Rs.5,000. SI at 4% for 2 years: 5000×4×2/100=400. SI at 6% for 2 years: 5000×6×2/100=600. Total SI=400+600=Rs.1,000. Shortcut: average rate = (4+6)/2 = 5%; Total SI = 10000×5×2/100=1000 ✓ (valid when amounts are equal). Trap: Rs.800 = 10000×4×2/100 (uses 4% only); Rs.1,200 = 10000×6×2/100 (uses 6% only).

questions.stem: Rs.2,000 earns Rs.800 as SI in 4 years. In how many years will Rs.3,000 earn Rs.1,800 as SI at the same rate?
A principal amount grows to Rs.950 in 3 years and Rs.1,100 in 6 years at Simple Interest. Find the principal.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SI for years 3 to 6 (3 years) = 1100−950 = 150. So SI per year = 150/3 = 50. SI for 3 years = 150. Principal = 950 − 150 = 800. Verify: P=800, SI/year=50, SI for 3 years=150; A₃=950 ✓; SI for 6 years=300; A₆=800+300=1100 ✓. Rate=50×100/800=6.25%. Trap: Rs.750 = 950−200 (wrong SI calculation); Rs.850 = midpoint error.
